executive_summary: EUR/SEK closed at 10.96619 on 2026-10-30, 2.95% lower over one month (krona stronger), 0.08% lower over three months, 0.76% higher over six months and 0.17% higher over a year, while USD/SEK at 9.82069 is 2.29% lower over the month but 3.19%, 5.79% and 3.94% higher over three, six and twelve months, after USD/SEK closed at a 52-week high of 10.05109 on 1 October, the krona's weakest level since April 2025 [16]. The dominant narrative is a Riksbank turning to hikes into an imported energy shock: all five Executive Board members moved hawkish in the September minutes, consensus expects a 25bp hike to 2.00% on 4 November, and the two-year government bond yield at 2.72% sits 97bp above the 1.75% policy rate, yet only about 17bp was priced for the meeting on 30 October [3][5][8][18]. Valuation is supportive: the BIS real effective rate fell to 93.36 in September, 5.31 points lower over a year and at the 12th percentile of its 33 monthly readings since January 2024 and the second-lowest index level in G10+SGD after the yen's 66.61, and the krona is 13.0% cheap to the dollar on World Bank PPP factors (latest annual vintage, about 2025, against 2026-10-30 spot; best available, flagged) [39][40]. The tension is that the inflation case for hiking is weak on the measure the Riksbank targets once energy is removed: CPIF rose to 1.5% in September but CPIF excluding energy was 0.5%, 0.2pp below the Riksbank's own forecast, while TTF gas at EUR100/MWh and Brent near $118 hurt Sweden's terms of trade and the 13 September election has left Sweden without a government after the Riksdag rejected the first prime-ministerial candidate 248-99 [5][26][31][32]. Against that, growth is the strongest in Europe outside Switzerland, with GDP up 2.8% over a year and 0.4% in Q3, a manufacturing PMI of 58.1 and business confidence at its strongest since 2022 [18], and SEB reports large short-krona positions that leave room for a short-covering rally [10][13][29]. We are Bullish tactically (weighted score +0.11, conviction 2, confidence 52%) with a four-week base case of EUR/SEK 10.85 and USD/SEK 9.72, because an underpriced hike and short positioning outweigh energy, politics and a firm dollar. We are Bullish strategically (+0.15, conviction 2, confidence 51%) with a six-month base case of EUR/SEK 10.75 and USD/SEK 9.60, resting on a 6.45%-of-GDP current account surplus, a cheap real exchange rate and AAA public finances, with the caveat that markets already price close to 100bp of tightening and a dovish surprise on 4 November or a snap election would undercut the call.

tactical.analysis: The Riksbank's policy rate is 1.75%, unchanged since September 2025 and held again on 24 September (decision published that day, minutes on 30 September), when the Board said the rate should be raised more than in the June forecast and that it expects to begin raising it this year [2]. It ranks eighth of the ten G10+SGD rate-setters, above only the BoJ (1.25%) and the SNB (0%), and sits 285bp below the RBA, 275bp below Norges Bank, 212.5bp below the Fed midpoint, 200bp below the BoE, 100bp below the RBNZ and 75bp below both the ECB and the Bank of Canada after the latter's 28 October hike. The minutes are explicit: Governor Thedeen called it reasonable to raise the rate as early as November, Deputy Governor Seim will advocate a first increase in November, First Deputy Governor Bunge sees a hike likely before year-end and Deputy Governor Hjelm sees 2.00% as reasonable during 2026 [3]. Consensus is a 25bp hike to 2.00% on 4 November, called by Nordea, SEB, Handelsbanken and ING, yet ING reports only about 17bp priced on 30 October, down from 22-24bp a week earlier after CPIF excluding energy undershot, with about 40bp priced for a February follow-up [5][9]. We put 75% on a hike, about 2bp more in expected value than is priced; delivery would force the remaining 8bp into the price and lift February pricing, while a hold would remove 17bp at once. The two-year government bond yield at 2.722% on 30 October is 97bp above the policy rate and has risen 78-79bp over a year, so further out the curve already prices the hiking cycle [18]. The krona pays negative carry against seven of nine peers, so the factor's tactical value is the expectations channel: a hike on 4 November is the only G10 central bank move in the window that is both likely and not fully priced. Tactically the factor is Bullish at modest confidence, because the Board's own words point to a hike that markets price at roughly two-in-three and carry is a modest 65-pip monthly cost against the euro.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the level of Swedish rates rises but the relative path is less clearly in the krona's favour, because the market already prices most of the cycle [5]. The September Monetary Policy Report path implies a Q4 2026 average of 1.85% and a Q1 2027 average of 2.07%, hikes continuing through 2027, then a gradual decline from 2028 towards the middle of the 1.5-3% neutral range [1][9]. Goldman expects quarterly hikes to 2.50%, ING expects 2.00% in November and 2.25% in February with hawkish risks, while Swedbank calls the roughly 100bp of tightening priced over the next year excessive because short mortgage fixing transmits hikes to households quickly [5][7][29]. Our base case is 2.00% in November, 2.25% by March 2027 and 2.50% by mid-2027, about 75bp of tightening over nine months, which is close to or slightly below what the two-year yield implies. Peers are hiking too: we expect the Fed at 4.00-4.25%, the ECB at 2.75-3.00%, the BoE at 4.00-4.25%, the BoJ at 1.50-1.75% and the RBNZ at 3.00% by March 2027, so the krona's negative carry narrows by 25-50bp against the euro and the krone but barely changes against the dollar and sterling. Carry against the euro would fall from -75bp to about -50bp, costing a krona long about 274 EUR/SEK pips over six months rather than 411, a modest drag. The SGB-Bund ten-year spread at -19.6bp already prices Swedish long rates close to German ones, so further convergence would need the Riksbank to out-hike the ECB beyond 2027. Strategically the factor is Neutral: the krona's rate disadvantage narrows, but the narrowing is largely in the curve and carry remains negative against most of G10.

tactical.analysis: Swedish data present a split between strong activity and soft underlying inflation, and the two offset each other for the krona over four weeks [10][11]. September CPI rose to 1.1% y/y from 0.3% and CPIF to 1.5% from 0.7%, the CPI reading the highest since February 2025, but both were driven by fuel (+20%) and electricity (+17%) while food prices fell 6.6% because of the temporary VAT cut [11]. CPIF excluding energy, the cleaner underlying measure, was 0.5%, 0.2pp below the Riksbank's own forecast [5], and the Riksbank estimates that the temporary fiscal measures hold CPIF about 1.5pp lower, putting CPIF ex-fiscal measures at 2.2% in August. Activity is strong: Q3 GDP rose 0.4% q/q against 0.3% expected after 1.6% in Q2, annual growth is 2.8%, the manufacturing PMI was 58.1 in September against a 54.6 forecast, and the NIER's business confidence rose to 110.7 from 109.3 [10][13]. Households are weaker: consumer confidence fell to 94.3 from 102.3, retail sales fell 0.4% in September, and consumer inflation expectations jumped to 7.7% from 6.3%, a warning sign for second-round effects [10]. The labour market is slack, with seasonally adjusted LFS unemployment at 8.7% in September, the highest in G10+SGD, although employment rose 54,200 over a year [12]; the Riksbank's September MPR forecasts NMO wage growth of 3.5% for 2026. PPI rose 11.2% y/y in September, so pipeline pressure is building even as core consumer inflation is soft [10]. The October CPIF flash on 5 November is the next test: ING expects CPIF to reach 2.5% and CPIF excluding energy 1.0% by December [5]. In our judgement a print at or below 0.5% excluding energy would challenge a second hike, which is why we keep the factor Neutral.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the growth and inflation mix favours the krona because Sweden combines Europe's fastest growth outside Switzerland with inflation that is set to rise towards and above target as the fiscal measures and the energy shock pass through [1][5]. The Riksbank forecasts GDP growth of 2.8% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027, against euro-area growth of 1.3% over the latest year, with resource utilisation returning to normal in early 2027 [1]. Its CPIF forecast rises from 1.5% in 2026 to 2.1% in 2027 and 2.4% in 2028, and CPIF excluding energy from 0.8% to 2.0% and 2.9%, with the war's indirect effects adding up to about 0.4pp in 2027 (best available, flagged, as of the 24 September MPR) [1]. ING expects CPIF excluding energy above 2.0% by summer 2027, and durable goods prices rose 1.1% in September with annual goods inflation positive for the first time in over a year [5]. Unemployment is forecast to fall from 8.6% in 2026 to 8.1% in 2027, so the slack that currently argues for caution should shrink through the horizon [1]. House prices rose 1.6% in September on the SBAB Booli index and are 5.5% below the spring-2022 peak, so the most rate-sensitive sector is recovering despite hike expectations [14]. The risk is that rate hikes into 8.7% unemployment and a 94.3 consumer-confidence reading bring a slowdown, which SEB flags as a downside risk to its 2027 growth outlook [29]. Strategically the factor is Bullish at low confidence: rising core inflation from a strong-growth base gives the Riksbank reason to keep hiking while peers slow.

tactical.analysis: Global risk appetite is mixed and turning more cautious into a dense event week, which leaves the factor without a clear signal for a mildly risk-on currency [36][19]. The VIX closed at 17.2 on 29 October, about the 52nd percentile of its one-year range and 46th of five years (percentiles best available, flagged, as of 2026-10-29), but traded at 20.05 at midday on 30 October as tanker attacks in Hormuz lifted oil, a 2.85-point jump in a session [31][36]. ICE BofA US high-yield spreads widened to 326bp on 29 October from 308bp on 29 September, +18bp, about the 95th percentile of the past year, and investment-grade spreads at 89bp are at about the 96th percentile (levels and percentiles best available, flagged, as of 2026-10-29), so credit is pricing more stress than equities. Swedish equities are resilient: the OMX Stockholm 30 closed at 3,271.40 on 30 October, up 1.39% in a month and 18.23% over a year, about 2.3% below its September all-time high of 3,349.50 [19]. The krona's risk beta runs through the European industrial cycle: Swedish manufacturing confidence of 111.5 and a PMI of 58.1 describe an export sector in expansion despite the energy shock [13]. The tail risks are concentrated in the next week: the US midterms on 3 November, which open a window for US strikes on Iran that the White House had said would not come before the polls, and a widening of credit spreads [31]. In a VIX spike above 25 the krona would underperform through its liquidity discount, as it did when it fell to its weakest level against the dollar since April 2025 on 1 October [16]. Tactically the factor is Neutral: equities and European business surveys support the krona, while credit and event risk argue for caution, and neither dominates.

strategic.analysis: Over six months risk appetite depends on the war and on central banks tightening into an energy shock, and the two risks are balanced for the krona [31][34]. A negotiated end to the US-Iran war, which Qatari mediators were working on in late October, would cut energy prices and lift European cyclicals, the krona's best environment [31]. A prolonged conflict with Brent above $110 and the Fed, ECB, BoE and Riksbank all hiking would tighten financial conditions and weigh on the high-beta end of G10, where the krona sits through its liquidity discount [33][34]. Credit spreads already at the 95th-96th percentile of the past year show that this second scenario is partly priced. Swedish equities' 18.2% gain over a year rests on industrial exporters that benefit from a weak krona, so a strong krona recovery would be partly offset by equity outflows if earnings guidance falls [19]. The krona's correlation with European risk remains intact: EUR/SEK fell as European business confidence rose, which supports a European-beta reading rather than a pure liquidity reading. We put the probability of a negotiated settlement by April 2027 at 35% and of a broader risk-off episode at 25%, which leaves the expected effect close to zero. Strategically the factor is Neutral at low confidence.

tactical.analysis: The krona has no CFTC series because there is no reportable Swedish krona futures contract in the Commitments of Traders data, so leveraged-fund and asset-manager net contracts, open interest and a positioning percentile do not exist and the factor rests on proxies. The clearest proxy is dealer commentary: SEB said on 20 October that investors hold large short-krona positions, leaving room for a sharp short-covering rally, and MUFG closed its long USD/SEK trade that week, saying the krona can rebound further after its September sell-off [29]. The price confirms the short was large: EUR/SEK fell 2.95% in October while hike pricing for 4 November fell from 22-24bp to about 17bp, so the rally ran ahead of rate expectations [5]. Speculators' gross dollar long across eight IMM futures was cut 11% to $40bn in the week to 20 October but remains historically elevated, so a broad dollar long is still in place against which the krona can gain [30]. Official flows are neutral: under the allocation set on 10 December 2025 and unchanged since, the Riksbank keeps its reserves at SEK584bn with USD 8bn and EUR 2bn hedged and has announced no foreign-currency sales or purchases for 2026, unlike the 2023 programme that was mechanically krona-positive [4]. Futures-implied rolls of -326.2bp for USD/SEK and -96.2bp for EUR/SEK on 29 October (best available, flagged) are wider than the policy gaps, consistent with expected Fed and ECB hikes and a funding premium for dollars and euros. NOK/SEK at the 98th percentile of its 52-week range shows the krona short is concentrated against the krone, where oil supports the other side. Tactically the factor is Bullish at low confidence: a crowded krona short meets a likely hike, which is the configuration that produced October's rally.

strategic.analysis: Over six months flows depend on whether foreign and domestic investors re-hedge into the krona once the energy shock fades, and the evidence is not yet decisive [4][29]. Swedish institutional investors hold large foreign portfolios, and higher Swedish rates raise the attraction of hedging foreign assets back into kronor, a krona-positive flow that tends to build gradually as the Riksbank tightens. The Riksbank's reserve hedges of USD 8bn and EUR 2bn, set on 10 December 2025, are unchanged for 2026 and no new programme has been announced, so there is no official flow to lean on [4]. On the Debt Office's 28 May forecast (best available, flagged, as of 2026-05-28; the next forecast is due on 26 November), government bond supply rises to SEK220bn of nominal issuance in 2026 and SEK240bn in 2027 from SEK118bn in 2025, with weekly auctions of SEK5bn since 17 June, which requires foreign demand at a 20bp discount to Bunds [23]. Without a CFTC contract the six-month positioning signal is limited to whether the krona short against the krone unwinds, which depends on oil rather than on Swedish fundamentals. The speculative dollar long of $40bn would be a krona-positive source of flow if it unwinds as the Fed approaches the end of its cycle [30]. Against that, a snap election or a sharper energy shock would rebuild the krona short quickly, because foreign investors treat the krona as a liquid proxy for European risk. Strategically the factor is Neutral: re-hedging and a possible dollar-long unwind are positives, heavier bond supply and the risk of rebuilt shorts are negatives.

factors.contrarian_analysis_tactical: Positioning is stretched short, on dealer evidence rather than CFTC data: SEB describes large short-krona positions and EUR/SEK only reached the 53rd percentile of its range after October's rally, while NOK/SEK is at the 98th. The unwind trigger is a 25bp hike on 4 November with a path that confirms a second hike, or a CPIF-excluding-energy print of 0.7% or higher on 5 November. A squeeze would be quick because the krona is illiquid outside European hours: we would expect EUR/SEK to fall 1-2% to 10.75-10.85 within a fortnight, similar to the 2.95% fall in October. The other side of the trade sees an energy importer without a government and with core inflation of 0.5%; we think that case is priced at 10.97.
factors.contrarian_analysis_strategic: Over six months positioning is not an independent driver: an unwound short leaves the krona dependent on rates, growth and energy. The contrarian risk is the opposite of the tactical one: if a krona long becomes the consensus after a hike, a dovish December path or a failed fourth prime-ministerial vote could rebuild shorts quickly. The 2023-24 episode, when the Riksbank's reserve hedging removed a short-krona overhang, shows that a positioning reset can add 3-5% to the krona over a few months, but no comparable official flow is in place now [4]. We treat positioning as neutral at this horizon.

tactical.analysis: Over four weeks the external factor works against the krona through energy prices, even though the underlying balance is strong [31][32]. TTF gas touched EUR100/MWh on 28 October for the first time since December 2022, about three times pre-war levels, with EU storage near 75% and German storage near 60% heading into winter [32]. Front-month TTF futures settled at EUR97.92 on 29 October against EUR72.36 on 30 September, a 35% rise in the month (best available, flagged, as of 2026-10-29). Brent's expiring front-month settled at $117.64 on 30 October, about 15% higher in the month, against the $92 end-2026 level ING says the Riksbank assumed in September [5][31]. Sweden is a net importer of oil and gas, so the direction is clear: rising TTF and Brent hurt Swedish terms of trade, and they help the krone, which is why NOK/SEK rose 2.29% in October to the 98th percentile of its range. The offset is that Sweden's electricity is mainly hydro and nuclear, so the gas shock reaches Swedish costs less directly than German ones, and copper futures were steady at $6.58/lb against $6.56 a month earlier (best available, flagged, as of 2026-10-29). The trade balance swung to a surplus of SEK4.1bn in September from a deficit in August first reported at SEK11.9bn, the largest since 2022 [10], and since revised to SEK12.8bn, so the monthly drag eased. The EU takes about 61% of Swedish exports (best available, flagged, latest available profile), with Germany the largest single market, so European industrial demand matters more for the krona than oil itself. Tactically the factor is Bearish: energy prices are rising into winter and the krona remains the energy-importing side of the Scandinavian pair.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the structural balance dominates and it favours the krona [15][1]. The current account surplus was SEK126.2bn in Q2 2026, up from SEK103.7bn a year earlier and SEK93.9bn in Q1, or 6.45% of GDP, the fourth-largest in G10+SGD after Norway, Singapore and Switzerland [15]. Its composition is robust to energy prices: the goods surplus fell to SEK67.7bn from SEK86.5bn a year earlier, but primary income rose to SEK100.9bn, of which SEK97.6bn was investment returns on Sweden's foreign assets, so the surplus now rests on income rather than on trade [15]. Energy is the risk to the trade component: Brent near $118 and TTF near EUR98 cut the goods surplus, but futures curves point lower over the horizon and a settlement, which we put at 35% by April 2027, would remove most of the premium [31][32]. The Riksbank expects the krona to strengthen again over its forecast period [1]. Valuation reinforces the surplus: the BIS real effective rate at 93.36 sits at the 12th percentile of its 33-month range, so the external balance is being earned at a cheap exchange rate [39]. European concentration is a vulnerability: with about 61% of exports going to the EU (best available, flagged), a German slowdown would hit the surplus harder than the energy price itself. Strategically the factor is Bullish at low confidence, because a large and income-driven surplus at a cheap real exchange rate should pull the krona higher once energy stops rising.

tactical.analysis: The Riksbank's communication since September has been unusually explicit and has moved hawkish across the whole Board, which supports the krona into 4 November [2][3]. The 24 September decision said the policy rate should be raised more than in the June forecast and that the Board expects to begin raising it this year if the outlook holds, and the September MPR adds that monetary policy would need to be adjusted if supply shocks combine with stronger demand [1][2]. The named minutes of the 23 September meeting, published on 30 September, show the shift by member: Governor Thedeen judged it reasonable to raise the rate as early as November, Deputy Governor Seim will advocate a November increase unless the outlook changes, Bunge sees a hike likely before year-end, Hjelm sees 2.00% as reasonable in 2026, and only Jansson argued for using the scope to wait [3]. Thedeen has since said there are strong reasons to raise rates in the near term, and the Board's explicit concern about the krona's weakness, which Bunge said also justifies tighter policy, ties the exchange rate directly into the reaction function [3][5]. Against that guidance, markets priced only about 17bp on 30 October, so the gap between what the Board has said and what is priced is roughly 8bp for this meeting [5]. The Riksbank's credibility in following through on explicit guidance is high, because its published path and named minutes make reversals costly. The Monetary Policy Update on 4 November will not carry a full new forecast, so the statement language on the next step is the signal; the minutes follow about two weeks later and the full Monetary Policy Report on 16 December. Tactically the factor is Bullish: the guidance points to a hike that is not fully priced, and a hawkish statement would add to it.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the guidance question is whether the Riksbank validates the roughly 100bp of tightening the curve prices, and here the market is ahead of the Board [9][29]. The September path, with averages of 1.85% in Q4 2026 and 2.07% in Q1 2027, implies about 50bp of tightening by early 2027, and the Board described the path as continuing to rise through 2027 [1][9]. Goldman's 2.50% terminal (Factor 1) and ING's 2.25% by February bracket that path, while the two-year yield implies more, and Swedbank argues that short mortgage fixing will limit how far the Board can go [5][29]. Hjelm called the rate path slightly high in September and Jansson preferred to wait, so the Board's two most cautious members would resist a faster pace if CPIF excluding energy stays near 0.5% [3]. Against that, the September MPR says monetary policy would need to be adjusted if supply shocks combine with stronger demand, and consumer inflation expectations of 7.7% in October [9] are the kind of signal that could trigger it [1]. The December Monetary Policy Report will update the path with Brent near $113 for January rather than the $92 assumed in September, which on its own argues for a higher path [5]. The net effect is that we expect a December path broadly in line with market pricing, not above it. Strategically the factor is Neutral: the Board's credibility is high, but its guidance is already priced and two members lean cautious.

tactical.analysis: Event risk over four weeks is concentrated and skewed against the krona, through Swedish politics and the war [26][27][31]. The 13 September election (results reported on 17 September) gave the four-party left bloc 176 of 349 seats against 173, but on 15 October the Riksdag rejected Magdalena Andersson as prime minister by 248 votes to 99, with the Left, Centre and Green parties voting against her [25][26]. A second vote on Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist is scheduled for 3 November and is expected to fail, after which the mandate passes to Moderate leader Ulf Kristersson; the Speaker has four proposals, and if all fail an extra election must be held within three months [26][27]. The caretaker government must present a rollover budget by 12 November, with amendments allowed until 27 November and a possible rival budget from the Tido parties [28]. The war is the second channel: two tankers were struck in Hormuz within 24 hours at the end of October, the White House had said it would not strike Iran before the 3 November midterms, and Qatari mediators were working on a deal [31]. A US strike would lift energy prices and the VIX, a double negative for the krona, while a deal would do the opposite. No implied volatility is observable for SEK pairs, so the event premium cannot be measured; EUR/SEK 20-day realised of 3.23% suggests the political risk is not being priced. Tactically the factor is Bearish at low confidence: the three nearest events - the 3 November prime-ministerial vote, the US midterms the same day and the budget by 12 November - each carry more downside than upside for the krona.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the political and geopolitical tails remain skewed against the krona, although the most likely outcome is a minority government formed by January [26][28]. If the Thand Ringqvist vote fails, Kristersson receives the mandate and would need the support or abstention of at least one centre party, which the 15 October vote showed is not available on the left side either [26]. An extra election would delay a full-year budget into spring 2027 and extend the caretaker rollover budget, which keeps 2026 spending levels plus indexation and a defence increase, so the fiscal impulse would be neutral but policy reform would stall [28]. The temporary food VAT and fuel tax cuts are assumed by the Riksbank to end by end-2027, and a new government's decision on extending them would shift the CPIF profile by up to 1.5pp, a source of rate-path uncertainty [1]. On the war, we put 35% on a negotiated settlement by April 2027, which would be strongly krona-positive through energy and risk, and 25% on an escalation that keeps Brent above $120 [31]. The US midterms and their aftermath could also revive tariff threats against Europe, which would hit Sweden's export sector given that the EU takes about 61% of its exports (best available, flagged). Weighted by probability, the political and war risks together carry a small negative expected value for the krona. Strategically the factor is Bearish at low confidence.

tactical.analysis: Sweden's sovereign position is among the strongest in G10 and is not a near-term driver of the krona, even with deficits rising [23][24]. Sweden is rated Aaa by Moody's and AAA by S&P, Fitch and Scope, as listed by the Debt Office (the page carries no dates of the latest agency actions; best available, flagged) [24]. The Debt Office's forecast of 28 May 2026 (best available, flagged, as of 2026-05-28; its next forecast is due on 26 November) puts general government (Maastricht) debt at 35% of GDP in 2025, 37% in 2026 and 39% in 2027, and central government debt at 19%, 21% and 23% of GDP [23]. The central government net borrowing requirement is forecast at SEK196bn in 2026 and SEK208bn in 2027, up from the previous forecast, and nominal bond issuance doubles to SEK220bn in 2026 from SEK118bn in 2025 [23]. Weekly SEK5bn auctions since 17 June have been absorbed without visible strain: the ten-year yield fell about 10bp in October to 3.123% and trades only 20bp below Bunds [17][23]. The caretaker budget due by 12 November rolls over 2026 spending with indexation and a defence increase, so it carries no new fiscal impulse and no consolidation [28]. consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: At three months our 10.80 is 2,000 pips (1.8%) below ING's 11.00 year-end target and 3,500 pips (3.1%) below its earlier 11.15 three-month forecast; at six months our 10.75 is 2,500 pips (2.3%) below ING's 11.00 six-month forecast; against the dollar our 9.60 at six months is 1,300 pips (1.3%) below ING's 9.73 and 1,700 pips below Trading Economics' Q4 9.77.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Forecasts set in early October were anchored to EUR/SEK near 11.20 and to a krona that the energy shock had pushed to its weakest level against the dollar since April 2025; they encode a slow recovery because external factors were judged to dominate the Riksbank [6]. We put more weight on the combination of an underpriced hike, a crowded short and a real exchange rate at the 12th percentile of its range, which together make the first leg of the recovery faster than the banks expect [5][29][39]. Consensus also underweights the shift in the current account towards primary income, which makes the surplus less sensitive to energy prices than in 2022 [15]. We share the banks' view that energy is the binding constraint, which is why our six-month target is only 1.6% below the forward.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: If we are right at 10.75, a krona long through the 10.9251 six-month forward earns about 1,751 pips, while a long EUR/SEK forward positioned for ING's 11.00 loses the same 1,751 pips instead of gaining about 749.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If ING is right at 11.00, a forward krona long at 10.9251 loses about 749 pips (0.7%); if the downside case of 11.35 materialises the loss is 4,249 pips, with the trigger an extra election or Brent above $125, and the krona's illiquidity would front-load that loss.

cleanest_bullish_expression.rationale: Short EUR/SEK is the cleanest krona-positive expression: it isolates the Riksbank-versus-ECB rate story, costs only 75bp of carry (about 65 pips a month), and the SGB-Bund ten-year spread of -19.6bp already shows Swedish rates converging on euro rates [17]. Structure is at an inflection, with spot on the 200-day average at 10.94 and support zones at 10.73-10.85 and 10.56, and French fiscal stress is an additional euro-specific headwind [6].

cleanest_bearish_expression.rationale: If the krona weakens, long NOK/SEK is the cleanest expression: it earns 275bp of carry, the most negative krona ratio in the set (-0.59 over 60-day realised), and captures the energy-escalation scenario in which TTF and Brent rise, hurting Sweden and helping Norway. The cross is at the 98th percentile of its range, so entries on dips towards 1.0341-1.0439 are better than chasing.

relative_value_pairs.thesis: The krona earns 175bp over the franc with the best krona carry ratio (+0.36), and CHF/SEK at 11.91 sits in the middle of its range; the franc's risk-off bid is the risk, so size small.

Sterling pays 200bp more, but GBP/SEK at the 88th percentile of its 52-week range and UK fiscal and energy exposure make it a six-month candidate for krona outperformance once the BoE's hiking cycle is priced.
Earns 50bp and benefits from a Riksbank hike, but the yen leads the strategic ranking, so we hold it only into 4 November.

cross_horizon_consistency.summary: Aligned: Bullish tactically (+0.11, conviction 2, confidence 52%) and Bullish strategically (+0.15, conviction 2, confidence 51%).
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: Both horizons are Bullish, but for different reasons. Tactically the call rests on the 4 November hike and short positioning, with energy, politics and the dollar against it; strategically it rests on the current account, growth and fiscal strength, with policy Neutral because the curve already prices the cycle. Confidence is a point lower strategically because the structural factors pay out only as energy prices ease.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 4 November decision is the tactical inflection; the 16 December Monetary Policy Report, which will show whether the path rises to meet market pricing, is the strategic one.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: A hold on 4 November would turn the tactical view Neutral and weaken the strategic view; a US-Iran settlement would lift both to conviction 3 or more.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Express both horizons through short EUR/SEK, adding after the 4 November decision rather than before it, and hold the strategic position through six-month forwards near 10.9251.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: USD/SEK: indicative forward points of -174, -522 and -1,043 pips give outrights of 9.8033, 9.7685 and 9.7164 at one, three and six months (krona forward premium about 2.1% annualised); against our expected 9.72, 9.66 and 9.60 the edge is 833, 1,085 and 1,164 pips krona-positive. ING's October forwards for EUR/SEK (11.19, 11.18 and 11.16 at one, three and six months from 11.20 spot) show the same small forward premium for the krona [6]. Forward points are indicative, derived by covered interest parity from the policy-rate differentials (75bp for EUR/SEK, 212.5bp for USD/SEK) with no basis adjustment; the futures-implied rolls observed on 2026-10-29 (best available, flagged) (-96.2bp for EUR/SEK, -326.2bp for USD/SEK) are wider and imply a slightly larger forward premium, consistent with expected Fed and ECB hikes and a funding premium, which cannot be split into rate expectations and basis without an OIS curve. Forwards therefore price the krona to strengthen about 0.75% a year against the euro and 2.1% against the dollar on carry alone. Our expected path is 1.0-1.6% below the EUR/SEK forwards, which is the edge; it comes from the Riksbank, short covering and valuation rather than from carry.

key_catalysts.event: Second prime-ministerial vote (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist); US midterm elections; RBA decision
key_catalysts.rationale: A failed vote, which SVT expects, passes the mandate to Kristersson and uses the second of four proposals before an extra election becomes mandatory. The midterms open the window in which US strikes on Iran become possible, which would lift energy prices and the VIX, both krona-negative.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially: the vote's failure is expected; an extra-election path and a US strike are not priced

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank policy decision and Monetary Policy Update
key_catalysts.rationale: Consensus expects a 25bp hike to 2.00%, the first of the cycle, backed by the Governor and Deputy Governor Seim in the September minutes. With about 17bp priced, delivery and a bias towards February would trigger short covering.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially: about 17bp (roughly 68%) priced on 30 October; about 40bp for February

key_catalysts.event: Sweden CPIF flash (October); Norges Bank and Bank of England decisions
key_catalysts.rationale: CPIF excluding energy at 0.7% or higher would validate the hike and lift February pricing; at 0.5% or lower it would revive doubts. A BoE hike widens GBP/SEK carry to -225bp and a Norges Bank hold keeps NOK/SEK carry at -250bp after a Riksbank hike.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially: a soft core print is expected after September's undershoot

key_catalysts.rationale: Consensus is +55k with unemployment at 4.2%; a strong report would lift December Fed hike odds above 80% and support USD/SEK, a weak one would weaken the dollar.

key_catalysts.event: Caretaker budget bill deadline; Sweden final CPI and registered unemployment (October)
key_catalysts.rationale: The rollover budget carries no new fiscal impulse; the risk is a rival Tido-party budget that signals a right-bloc government or a breakdown towards an extra election. Final CPI confirms the flash; registered unemployment is the Public Employment Service measure, distinct from the Labour Force Survey rate due on 20 November.

The LFS rate was 8.7% seasonally adjusted and 8.1% unadjusted in September; a fall below 8.5% would support the Riksbank's forecast of shrinking slack, a rise above 9.0% would strengthen the cautious members' case for a pause.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank minutes of the 4 November meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: Named minutes show whether Jansson and Hjelm joined the hike and how many members favour a February follow-up. A majority for further hikes would lift February pricing towards 25bp.

key_catalysts.event: Deadline for budget amendments in the Riksdag
key_catalysts.rationale: Parties can table amendments until 27 November; a coordinated alternative budget would show whether a majority exists for any government, and therefore whether an extra election is likely.

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision (with SEP); Bank of Canada and RBNZ decisions
key_catalysts.rationale: A Fed hike to 4.00-4.25% would widen USD/SEK carry against the krona and add to year-end dollar demand.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially: about 77% priced for a hike

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank decision and Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The new path will incorporate Brent near $113 for January rather than $92 and the October CPIF, and we expect it to confirm further hikes in 2027. A path below 2.25% for mid-2027 would disappoint a curve pricing about 100bp.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially: the curve prices more than the September path

key_catalysts.event: ECB decision with projections; Norges Bank MPR; BoE decision
key_catalysts.rationale: An ECB hike to 2.75% keeps the EUR/SEK policy gap at 75bp after a Riksbank hike in November; a hold would favour the krona. Norges Bank's path sets NOK/SEK carry into 2027.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially: a December ECB hike is the base case in ING's outlook

key_catalysts.rationale: ING expects CPIF at 2.5% and CPIF excluding energy at 1.0% in December, which would confirm the turn in underlying inflation the Riksbank forecasts.

key_catalysts.event: Possible extra-election deadline window if all four prime-ministerial proposals fail
key_catalysts.rationale: If four proposals fail an extra election must be held within three months, delaying a full-year budget into spring and adding a political premium to the krona.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank decision and Monetary Policy Update
key_catalysts.rationale: ING and Goldman both expect a second hike to 2.25% around this meeting; about 40bp was priced for February on 30 October.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank decision and Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The March path will show whether the cycle extends towards 2.50% or stops; with the temporary fiscal measures due to end by end-2027, the CPIF profile for 2027-28 is the key input.

invalidators.condition: If the Riksbank holds at 1.75% on 4 November, would turn Neutral because the expectations channel that carries Factor 1 and Factor 6 tactically would reverse and the short-krona position would rebuild.
invalidators.mechanism: A hold removes about 17bp of pricing at once and turns the two largest tactical contributors Neutral, taking the net score below zero.

invalidators.condition: If October CPIF excluding energy prints 0.4% or lower on 5 November, would turn Neutral because a second hike would be priced out and the Board's cautious members would gain ground.
invalidators.mechanism: A falling core rate weakens the case for the path the curve prices and lowers February pricing below 20bp.
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: CPIF excluding energy at or below 0.4% y/y

invalidators.condition: If TTF front-month gas closes above EUR115/MWh for five sessions, would turn Bearish because Sweden's terms of trade would deteriorate faster than rate hikes can offset.
invalidators.mechanism: Higher gas prices widen Sweden's import bill and favour the krone, turning Factor 5 Bearish at both horizons.

invalidators.condition: If the Speaker's fourth prime-ministerial proposal fails and an extra election is called, would turn Bearish because the political premium would rise and the 2027 budget would be delayed into spring.
invalidators.mechanism: An extra election extends the caretaker period and adds a risk premium to an illiquid currency, turning Factor 7 more Bearish and Factor 8 Neutral strategically.

invalidators.condition: If EUR/SEK closes above 11.17 for two sessions, would turn Neutral because the October rally would have failed at the 50- and 100-day averages and the summer range would be restored.
invalidators.mechanism: A close above the 11.0761-11.1721 zone signals that short covering is complete and trend-following flows are krona-negative again.

invalidators.condition: If the VIX closes above 25 and US high-yield spreads widen beyond 375bp, would turn Bearish because the krona's liquidity discount dominates in risk-off.
invalidators.mechanism: A risk-off episode turns Factor 3 Bearish and amplifies the USD Liquidity drag, overwhelming the rate signal for an illiquid currency.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: VIX and ICE BofA US High Yield OAS
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: VIX above 25 and HY OAS above 375bp

invalidators.condition: If the December Monetary Policy Report path peaks below 2.25%, would turn Neutral strategically because the curve's roughly 100bp of tightening would be priced out.
invalidators.mechanism: A path below market pricing turns Factor 6 Bearish strategically and removes the rate support behind the growth case.

change_since_last_report.summary: Compared with the 2026-10-01 dossier, the tactical stance moves from Bearish (conviction 2, -0.21, rank 8) to Bullish (conviction 2, +0.11, rank 3), and the strategic stance stays Bullish but conviction falls from 3 to 2 (+0.26 to +0.15, rank 3 to 2).

factors_changed.reason: The Board's minutes moved the November hike from possible to guided, while market pricing fell to about 17bp, leaving an underpriced hike.
The two-year yield now sits 97bp above the policy rate, so most of the cycle is priced and peers are hiking too.
Unchanged: strong Q3 GDP and PMI offset CPIF excluding energy 0.2pp below the Riksbank forecast.
Equities and European business confidence improved; credit and event risk keep it from turning Bullish.
Dealer evidence of a large short-krona position meeting a likely hike; the October rally showed the short covering.
Unchanged: TTF rose from about EUR72 to EUR98 in October.
The Q2 current account rose to SEK126.2bn on primary income, making the surplus less energy-sensitive, and the September trade balance returned to surplus.
The curve has run ahead of the Board's published path, so guidance is priced.
The Riksdag rejected the first prime-ministerial candidate 248-99 on 15 October, raising extra-election risk.
French fiscal stress makes Swedish AAA status a relative support.
EUR/SEK fell through its 50- and 100-day averages to the 200-day; structure is no longer krona-negative.
Unchanged: a December Fed hike is about 77% priced.

seasonality.pattern: Year-end brings seasonal dollar funding demand and thinner liquidity in low-liquidity G10 currencies, and the krona has typically been among the currencies that weaken into the turn and recover in January as balance sheets reset.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: We do not attach a reliable average return to the pattern; it is a liquidity effect that adds to downside in the last week of November and December rather than a directional driver.
seasonality.current_alignment: Partly against the tactical Bullish view: it is captured in the Bearish USD Liquidity factor and in the path expectation's late-November pause, and it is aligned with the strategic staircase that consolidates through year-end before falling from February.

assumptions: Spot levels, moving averages, ranges, percentiles, average true ranges and realised volatility are from weekday closing bars to 2026-10-30; realised volatility is annualised on 252 days and the carry-to-volatility ratios use 60-day realised volatility, with no implied-volatility ratio because no SEK option quote was available.

Policy rates are the latest official settings: Riksbank 1.75%, Federal Reserve 3.75-4.00% (3.875% midpoint), ECB deposit rate 2.50%, BoJ 1.25%, BoE 3.75%, SNB 0%, Bank of Canada 2.50% after its 28 October hike, RBA 4.60%, RBNZ 2.75% and Norges Bank 4.50%; Singapore runs an exchange-rate band, so no SGD policy rate or carry is computed.

Market pricing for the Riksbank (about 17bp for 4 November and about 40bp for February) is ING's description of 30 October; no Swedish OIS strip was available, so the two-year government bond yield is used as the curve's summary of expected policy.

Swedish ten-year and peer ten-year yields are 30 October closes from one source, except France, which the source dates 1 November; for the US, Japan and Australia the comparator yields are the 30 October closes (best available, flagged), because the source page had already updated those three to 2 November.
No CFTC series exists for the krona; positioning is assessed from dealer commentary, futures-implied rolls, cross-rate percentiles and Riksbank reserve policy.

Forward points are indicative and derived by covered interest parity from policy-rate differentials with no basis adjustment; futures-implied rolls (best available, flagged, observed 2026-10-29) are reported alongside as a market cross-check.

PPP deviations use World Bank PPP factors (latest annual vintage, about 2025) applied to 2026-10-30 spot (best available, flagged); NZD/SEK spot for that comparison is the product of the NZD/NOK and NOK/SEK closes because no direct quote exists.

Peer CPI and core CPI are national September releases; Swedish and peer GDP, unemployment and current-account figures are the OECD and Eurostat vintages published by 2026-10-31, except Swedish unemployment, which is Statistics Sweden's September LFS rate (8.7% seasonally adjusted).

Brent and TTF levels are futures prints from 29-30 October (TTF and copper settlements best available, flagged, as of 2026-10-29); Brent's expiring December contract ($117.64) and the January contract ($113.43) are both reported because they diverged by about $4.

Scenario probabilities, the 75% probability of a 4 November hike and the probabilities for a US-Iran settlement (35% by April 2027) and an extra election (15% by January, about 20% by spring) are our estimates.
